name: Richard J. Durbin

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: The issue was the cost of prescription drugs and why they are so high.
And we wanted to discuss why prescription drugs cost so much in America.
And the question is, What if it became the American health insurance plan like Social Security is the American pension plan?
You can decide to buy more pension protection if you wish, but virtually all workers in America qualify for this one program, Social Security.
What if we did the same thing for Medicare and had what many have said is Medicare for All?
Well, Social Security seems to be a good basis of retirement for millions of Americans.

During the time that I have been in the Senate--30 years now--I would say the most important vote I ever cast was for Barack Obama's ObamaCare, as his critics call it, but we call it the Affordable Care Act.

And although I disagree with him, I hope that the new Congress that starts in just a few weeks is going to tackle this issue to bring down the cost of prescription drugs and to make healthcare affordable for more and more people.

He has also been one of my strongest friends and allies in the fight to pass the Dream Act--a measure which I introduced 25 years ago that said if you are brought to the United States as a child and you grew up here and you didn't get in trouble and you did what you were supposed to do, you ought to have a pathway to citizenship.
He was born in New Delhi, India, before immigrating to the United States and eventually settling in Peoria.
Congressman Krishnamoorthi, shortly after being sworn in, joined protests at O'Hare when President Trump, in his first term, implemented his Muslim travel ban.
Closest to my heart were his efforts to fight the vaping epidemic.

I finally tested that issue on the floor of the House of Representatives, and it turns out that the House is one of the largest frequent flyer clubs in America, and they were as sick and tired of secondhand smoke in airplanes as I was.

At the time I passed that measure banning smoking on airplanes, 29 percent of high school students in America were smoking tobacco cigarettes--29 percent; today, 2 percent--2 percent--smoking tobacco cigarettes.
I want to thank Raja Krishnamoorthi because he has taken up this cause with the new insidious effort by the tobacco companies to addict our children with vaping.
You have seen the vaping devices and all of these flavors that they sell their cigarettes in.
He led the first-ever congressional investigation into the matter in 2019--he chaired--and he pushed for bans on flavored vaping products.
In Congress, she fought passionately for a reasonable gun control law, authorizing the first-ever congressional analysis of the American gun violence epidemic.
She has been a leader on countless issues from the Affordable Care Act to human rights overseas.
He helped push for the passage of the Affordable Care Act and key provisions for federally qualified community health centers.
The issue is what we are going to do with healthcare in America.

And one of the reasons that I voted for it--and I have given this speech on the floor and I won't repeat it--is, if you have ever been a father of a sick baby and didn't have health insurance and took that baby to the hospital, you will never forget it.
I will tell you this: The healthcare providers that I talk to in Illinois are sick and tired of fighting with insurance companies for payment.
Years ago when I was a Member of the House of Representatives, I introduced a measure--just a little amendment--that banned smoking on airplanes.

statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Pursuant to rule XXII, the Chair lays before the Senate the pending cloture motion, which the clerk will state.

The bill clerk read as follows: Cloture Motion We, the undersigned Senators, in accordance with the provisions of rule XXII of the Standing Rules of the Senate, do hereby move to bring to a close debate on Calendar No. 453, H.R. 2347, a bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any damages, other than punitive damages, received on account of any sexual acts or sexual contact.
This January marks the 25th anniversary of the opening of detention camps for suspected terrorists at Guantanamo Bay.
The expressed purpose of sending captured suspects to Guantanamo was to detain them in a legal black hole.
Our nation's leaders wanted a place where detainees could be held and interrogated beyond the reach of our laws, our courts, our Constitution, and our ideals of justice and dignity.
Detainees were tortured and subjected to unspeakable abuse at Guantanamo, as well as at secret CIA black sites around the world.
Most were held in indefinite detention without charges or trial.
The few who were charged were in makeshift military commissions.
Twenty-five years after the attacks, the 9/11 trial still has not begun, and key confessions have been ruled too tainted by torture to be admissible in the court or a hearing.
For all of these reasons, I have held hearings, introduced legislation, and I came to this floor dozens of times, over the years, to push for the closure of Guantanamo.
Four years ago, I chaired a full committee hearing in the Senate Judiciary Committee about the urgent need to restore the rule of law by closing Guantanamo and resolving, finally, these cases.
Instead, we left the Guantanamo playbook open and available for President Trump and Stephen Miller.

Trump vowed during his Presidential campaign in 2016 that he would not only keep Guantanamo open but he would also ``load it up with some bad dudes.'' And now, in his second term, the President is making good on his threat by sending immigrants to this grotesque facility.
Most are migrants who have come to America seeking safety from persecution and torture, or simply a better life.
Victor escaped years of torture and abuse at the hands of MS-13 and law enforcement in El Salvador.
An immigration judge granted him withholding of removal to El Salvador based on his credible fear of torture if he returned.
After months of confinement in the United States, our government decided to send Mr. Alvarez to Guantanamo.
The administration has sent an estimated 25,000 people to third countries, denying them due process and legal protection against persecution and torture.
Many like Victor risk being returned to torture.

With the new year and a new Congress on the horizon, I hope our next generation of leaders will continue to fight for the ideals that made this Nation great and finally close the Guantanamo detention facility.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DREAMERS
statements.title: DREAMERS
sentences: Mr. President, it has been 25 years since I first came to the Senate floor with a simple request--for Congress to protect the Dreamers.
Dreamers are immigrants who were brought to the United States as children.
My office first heard about her case when she was unable to fill out her college application forms because she didn't have a Social Security number.
We learned that Tereza, under the law, would have to leave the United States for 10 years and then reapply for legal status.
I couldn't believe there was no path to citizenship for a young person like her, so I decided to introduce a bill to change it.
I joined forces with Republican Senator Orrin Hatch of Utah, and, together, we introduced the DREAM Act.
Since then, I have come to the floor of the Senate over 150 times to share the stories of Dreamers who are doctors, nurses, business owners, educators, parents, and members of our military.

Over the years, the Senate has passed the DREAM Act, which was included in that bill, and the House of Representatives has passed it too, but never at the same time so that we can send the legislation to the President's desk to be signed into law.
I am not going to give up on the Dreamers.
In fact, the first time I ever spoke to the President, it was about the Dreamers.
I ask the President of the United States now to keep his word, work with us to pass the Dream Act and do it now.
In fact, 81 percent of Americans support citizenship for Dreamers, including 56 percent of Republicans.
They led her on the path to becoming an organizer for the Service Employees International Union, or SEIU, representing the States of Illinois and Indiana.
Since 2019, Brenda has served as a representative of more than 90,000 home care workers in essential jobs--home care, childcare, nursing homes, and hospitals--90,000 workers.
This is who we might lose if we fail to pass the Dream Act.
No. She is one of hundreds of thousands of Dreamers who serve our country every day, even as they worry about being forced to leave this Nation.
We have an opportunity to finally give Dreamers the justice they deserve.

statements.title: Judicial Nominations (Executive Session)
sentences: There is an individual who was running in the election that just was completed on November 3, and he was running for reelection to the Texas Supreme Court.
The consolation prize for losing his race for the Texas Supreme Court was to give him a lifetime appointment to the Federal bench.
It was a lifetime experience that I will never forget.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SURVIVOR JUSTICE TAX PREVENTION ACT--Motion to Proceed--Continued
statements.title: SURVIVOR JUSTICE TAX PREVENTION ACT--Motion to Proceed--Continued
sentences: They were countries like Belarus, Haiti, Venezuela, Cuba, Ukraine, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
While several nations that emerged from the former Yugoslavia have prospered--joining the European Union and even NATO--others have struggled and still merit U.S. and European attention.
My visit reaffirmed my belief that we must continue to support efforts to draw these new nations into the EU and NATO and encourage the accompanying governance and economic reforms.
It is our duty to continue to defend the larger peace, prosperity, and democracy that emerged from so much conflict in Europe--a peace that is now threatened again by none other than Vladimir Putin.
Ukraine Mr. President, this leads me to the ongoing war in Ukraine--a war President Trump said he would end on his first day if he was reelected to the White House.

I don't begrudge President Trump's attempts to seek diplomatic solutions to this conflict, but it is long overdue that he realizes that you can't coddle Vladimir Putin and compel him to reach an accord.
The President has rolled out the red carpet for Putin on American soil.
Trump publicly scolded Ukraine for fighting for its life and its existence.
While President Trump belittles our allies and befriends our enemy, he is also trying to entice Putin with business deals as if this is some kind of a real estate scheme that we are talking about.
Vladimir Putin is a former KGB agent motivated not by money, but by warped historical grievances and perceived slights.

He is the same Russian leader who provided targeting information to Iran to destroy American assets and kill American troops in the Middle East--the same leader empowering a nuclear-armed North Korean regime that also threatens the United States.
Attempts to pacify Putin are both fantasy and folly by an American President who seems forever enamored by this autocratic Russian leader who is endlessly playing President Trump for a fool.
So as I wind down my time in Congress, let me implore the President and this new Congress: Don't give up on Ukraine.

We must help it restock its air defenses, make sure bipartisan appropriated funds are finally delivered instead of being delayed, sanctions waivers are ended, and that the Ukrainians have what they need to force Putin to a real negotiating table.
We need to pick sides in the Ukrainian war, and there is only one side that is consistent with America's values, and that is the side of the Ukrainian people.
After my recent visit to the Balkans--and many other trips to the Baltics--reminded me, we have to stay steadfast in our commitment to mutual defense in NATO.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: They have marched and bled to change the document so the promise of a more perfect Union would be available to all men and women, not just the few.
Over 20 years ago, I introduced a bill called the DREAM Act.

If you came to the United States as a child, if your parents brought you here in the backseat of a car, crossed into this country, and they did not file the necessary documents so that you were legal in America, under the DREAM Act, you would still have a chance of a pathway to citizenship.

The DREAM Act led to DACA, which was an Executive order of President Obama, and 830,000 young people who were brought to the United States went through a serious criminal background check and found nothing wrong, paid their fees, and submitted themselves to our government.
Madam President, 830,000 qualified for DACA.
There is a question now on moving forward on DACA and the DREAM Act.
I am willing to work with the President and anyone in the White House who wants to make sure we pass the DREAM Act before the end of this year.
I see presiding over the Senate one of my colleagues from South Carolina whose brother was a cosponsor of mine on the DREAM Act.
Now we have an opportunity--I hope we have an opportunity--to have Lisa Murkowski, my current cosponsor of the DREAM Act, to join me in seeing this finally become law.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ELECTIONS
statements.title: ELECTIONS
sentences: The President's subversion efforts came to a head on January 6, 2021, when an armed mob, that he incited, stormed the Capitol in an attempt to disrupt the peaceful transition of power.

Yet last week, the Supreme Court's conservative majority permitted part of this dangerous plan to move forward, allowing States to use the flawed database to verify the citizenship of registered voters.
Additionally, the Division has sent letters to election officials across the country threaten to file criminal charges against officials if a noncitizen casts a ballot in an upcoming election.
It is indeed frightening to watch this weaponization of Federal law enforcement.
While the Trump administration has had some victories, like the case before the Supreme Court last week, most of their interference efforts have been shut down by the Federal judiciary.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Doesn't that sound quaint these days, when we have a President who, in his first year of his second Presidential term, made $1.4 billion from his investments, particularly with the cryptocurrency bunch?

The most recent one that was reported was just 2 weeks ago when Donald Trump, Jr., had his wedding reception on some island somewhere, and it leaked to the press that the entire festivity reception was paid for by a Russian oligarch who is close to Vladimir Putin.

We are virtually at war with Putin and Russia for their invasion of Ukraine, and the son of the President of the United States gets married, goes to a private island for a lavish reception, and it is paid for by a Russian oligarch.
As my colleague Senator John Curtis, Republican of Utah, said when he heard of this: You expect a toaster for a wedding gift; you don't expect a Russian oligarch to pay for the reception.
Well, it is the case because we are in the eighth month of the first year of President Trump's war in Iran.
Do you remember when he came to the American people and said he was going to invade Iran?
He ignored the Constitution, which gives Congress the power to declare war, and went forward and invaded and attacked Iran.

Every day you fill up your gas tank, a trucker fills up their diesel tank, a farmer goes out in the field--and we are harvesting now in Illinois--and sees the cost of diesel fuel, every day, you remember this is a creation of the President of the United States for a war that was unnecessary, illegal, and didn't follow the Constitution at its outset.
The President has reported over 40 times that we have Iran on the ropes, that they can't wait to negotiate a settlement, and it never happens.
Where have they been for 8 months while we have been having these votes on the floor as to whether Congress approves of the war of Iran?

Rescissions Madam President, on Friday night, the Trump administration announced the President has unilaterally rescinded nearly $1 billion in funds Congress had approved for spending on a bipartisan basis.
Last year, President Trump canceled $4.9 billion in foreign aid with his so-called pocket rescission maneuver.
Earlier in 2025, my Republican colleagues supported President Trump's rescission request that clawed back $9 billion in foreign aid and public broadcast funding.
Rescission requests are made under a fast-track process in which a President can request Congress to rescind Federal funding with a simple majority vote in each Chamber.
However, President Trump--surprise--is attempting an unlawful maneuver called the pocket rescission.
The Government Accountability Office has stated that the President's pocket rescissions are illegal.
Democrats fought for pocket rescission protection in the continuing resolution we passed earlier this year to prevent the White House from doing exactly what they have done.
Taxpayer-funded political ads of the wartime President looking very resolute are a must.
In 2020, President Trump spent months spreading the Big Lie that the 2020 election was stolen.
This culminated in the January 6 attack on the Capitol, where President Trump's supporters tried to violently prevent the constitutional certification of the 2020 election.

I was here, right here at my desk when this happened, when the mob started coming into this Chamber, and we filed out that door with police protection to avoid this effort to overturn the 2020 election.

Instead of condemning this egregious criminal conduct on January 6, my Republican colleagues are spreading baseless conspiracy theories and attacking career prosecutors and FBI agents, claiming the so-called deep state is out to get Donald Trump--the deep state.
You remember the classified information that was found near the bathroom in Mar-a-Lago?
I am happy and content with my answers, and I will do it again if necessary.
And I will sit right next to Donald Trump, Jr. We can both testify under oath as to our personal experiences.
If this hearing is really about getting answers, we will finally get our chance--Jack Smith will get his chance to tell his side of the story under oath.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: I couldn't believe, when we looked up the law, that our Nation had no path to citizenship for a young person like her so I introduced a bill to change it.
Together, Senator Hatch and I introduced the DREAM Act.
Two senators of opposing parties, who didn't agree on much, came together to work on legislation to provide a pathway to legal status for these young people brought to the United States as children.
These young people came to be known as Dreamers.

Since I first introduced the DREAM Act, I have come to the Senate floor over 150 times to share the stories of these Dreamers, who, today, are doctors, nurses, business owners, educators, parents, and so many other professions.
Over the years, the DREAM Act has passed the Senate and it has passed the House, but never at the same time so that we couldn't send it to the President's desk to have it signed into law.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Freedom of the Press (Executive Session)
statements.title: Freedom of the Press (Executive Session)
sentences: At the same time, he launched an unprecedented number of baseless defamation lawsuits against respected news outlets for their factual reporting on his failed businesses, his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, and his role in the January 6, 2021, insurrection right here in this Capitol.
It is something you would expect to read about in the communist Russia days with Pravda and Izvestia or perhaps in North Korea, but not in the United States.
This assault on the press is a dangerous effort by the President to distract American public opinion away from his failed agenda, his endless Iranian war, and his self-defeating tariffs.
Chastising CNN won't lower the price of diesel fuel; punishing POLITICO won't end the Iranian war; and maligning MS NOW won't save the President's free-falling approval ratings.
I urge all my colleagues to speak out against this ban and the President's continued assault on the free press.

sentences: DOD is increasing its investments in medical research, and that is a good thing, I have been a supporter of that myself, when I chaired the subcommittee of appropriations on defense spending.
Senator Sasse was candid, honest, and levelheaded in saying this is considered a death sentence, but we are going to fight it.
Later this afternoon, I will take an airplane ride from Washington to Chicago.

Once again, as I have done hundreds of times--literally thousands of times--I will entrust my safety, my future, and my survival to a competent aircrew, as well as the air traffic controllers of America.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Nomination of Kasdin Miller Mitchell (Executive Session)
statements.title: Nomination of Kasdin Miller Mitchell (Executive Session)
sentences: She also represented the New York State Rifle & Pistol Association in the 2022 Supreme Court case New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen, which led to gun safety laws across the country being struck down.
Ms. Mitchell previously litigated against reproductive rights, and she argued for gutting the Voting Rights Act in a brief she submitted in Shelby County v. Holder.
I oppose her nomination and ask my colleagues to join me.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Nomination of Matthew R. Byrne (Executive Session)
statements.title: Nomination of Matthew R. Byrne (Executive Session)
sentences: While serving as a visiting justice on the Ohio Supreme Court, he objected to the court's dismissal of a case defending the State's abortion ban even after voters' decision to enshrine reproductive rights in the Ohio Constitution.
While campaigning to be a State court judge, Judge Byrne stated that he opposed abortion for any reason other than to protect the life of the mother.

He opposed exceptions for rape or incest and further wrote: ``I believe the `life of the mother' should be strictly defined so as to avoid creating loopholes.'' Judge Byrne's extreme views extend beyond his opposition to reproductive rights.

Nearly 5 years after the Supreme Court recognized the right to same-sex marriage, he stated that he still believed the judiciary does not possess the authority to expand the definition of marriage to include anything but one man and one woman.
I oppose his nomination and urge my colleagues to join me.

statements.title: Department of Homeland Security (Executive Calendar)
sentences: We are going to arrest them, and if they are not properly documented, we are going to deport them.
His children were forced to enter foster care because of his murder.
He said, ``Attack our law enforcement, and this FBI will find you and bring you to justice.'' Tough talk when the video shows that this young woman did not engage in any illegal conduct.
Why do we want to deport them back to situations that could be the scene of the crime for the very reasons that they came to the United States?
When it comes to the Dream Act, I will continue to fight for that as long as I can stand on this floor of the Senate, and, thereafter, if necessary.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE SEPTEMBER 11, 2001 ATTACKS
statements.title: 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE SEPTEMBER 11, 2001 ATTACKS
sentences: And across the border to our north, Canadians opened their homes, schools, and churches to house and care for more than 30,000 stranded travelers from hundreds of flights that were diverted due to the closure of American airspace.
Twenty-five years later, relations between the U.S. and Canada are strained due to the President's trade war, but we will never forget the generosity of our neighbors.

More than 3,000 children lost a parent that day--parents who had left home that morning for work or the firefighter, police officer, and other first responder parents who were off duty but rushed to the scene to help.

Ukraine Mr. President, on another unrelated topic--well, it is related, but it is different.
The war in Ukraine has turned a good corner for us, with the real possibility for the first time in over 4 years that Russia will be finally forced to negotiate.

I was at the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkiye, earlier this month with several colleagues, including Senators Shaheen and Coons, the late Lindsey Graham, and Senator Rounds, and the message was clear: Momentum is with Ukraine, and this is the time for American and European support to step up.

Unfortunately, too many of these air defenses have been needed in the gulf for President Trump's other war in Iran, and Ukraine still has not received $400 million we appropriated in last year's appropriations bill, signed into law by the President.
I asked Secretary Hegseth why the Pentagon is taking so long to send this critical aid to Ukraine.
They are desperately needed in Ukraine to stop the Russian advances.
Doing so will help bring President Putin to the negotiating table.

Secretary Hegseth also needs to move the $200 million we appropriated and the President signed into law for the Baltic Security Initiative to help frontline NATO allies prepare for Russian intimidation and retaliation.
My last point is this: It is overdue for this Chamber to act on Russia and Ukraine and the legislation which Lindsey Graham was passionate about.
